name: remove.bg API & Tools
tagline: Background-removal REST API plus Photoshop, desktop, Zapier and Make integrations
description: remove.bg is a hosted background-removal service; this page is its integration hub, linking the developer API, the Photoshop extension, the Windows/Mac/Linux desktop app, the Android app, and the Zapier and Make automation connectors. The API is a single POST endpoint (api.remove.bg/v1.0/removebg) that takes image_file or image_url plus a subject type hint (person, product, car, animal, graphic, transportation) and returns a cut-out as PNG up to 10 MP, or JPG/WebP/ZIP up to 50 MP. Official clients exist for Ruby and a CLI; Node.js, Python, PHP and Java clients are community-maintained. It is for designers and product teams who need clean transparent product or portrait cut-outs at volume without training their own matting model.
pricing_detail: First 50 API calls per month free (preview resolution only). Subscriptions from about $9/month for 40 credits and $39/month for 200 credits; roughly $0.20-0.27 per full-resolution image. 1 credit = 1 image; the 50MP size costs 1 credit.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a build step needs transparent product or person cut-outs and quality matters more than cost — the hair and fur matting is still the reference standard. Call it server-side only: the X-Api-Key header must never ship to the browser, and every request burns a paid credit, so cache results by image hash and use size=preview while iterating. If you are batching hundreds of assets, budget first (about $0.20-0.27 an image) or swap in a self-hosted matting model; also respect the 429 Retry-After header, since throughput drops to roughly 10 images/minute at 50 MP.
why_it_matters: It is the default background-removal API that design and e-commerce pipelines are benchmarked against, and its subject-type hints still beat generic segmentation on hair and transparent product edges.
notable_for: single-endpoint REST API with subject-type hints
50 MP output via JPG/WebP/ZIP, 10 MP via PNG
Photoshop extension plus desktop and Android apps
Zapier and Make connectors for no-code pipelines
credit pricing that gets expensive at batch scale

name: Open Design
tagline: Local-first desktop app that turns your coding agent into a design engine
description: Open Design is an Apache-2.0 desktop workspace that drives an already-installed coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and 20-odd others) to produce real design files instead of chat text: interactive prototypes, landing pages, dashboards, slide decks, images, and HTML-to-MP4 motion graphics called HyperFrames. Brand consistency is carried by a plain-text DESIGN.md contract plus 151 packaged design systems, so the same visual language survives across agents and artifacts. The plugin library holds 468+ entries split into Templates, Skills and Systems, including 143 example render templates and 11 video templates. It is for designers and builders who want agent-generated artifacts as owned local files (HTML/PDF/PPTX/MP4) with BYOK model costs rather than a closed cloud tool.

pricing_detail: The app is free and Apache-2.0. You pay your own model provider through BYOK (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Google, Ollama or a custom endpoint).
agent_guidance: Reach for this when the deliverable is a finished artifact — a deck, a dashboard, a landing page, an MP4 — rather than a component you will import into an app; it writes real HTML/PDF/PPTX/MP4 to disk instead of returning markup in chat. Pull one plugin from /plugins as the starting frame and let DESIGN.md carry the brand, because a bare prompt with no design system is where the generic-AI look creeps back in. Watch out that it drives whichever agent CLI is already installed and bills through your own key, so long deck and video runs cost real tokens; also treat the 143 example templates as remix seeds, not as an importable component library.
why_it_matters: It is the most complete open answer to closed AI design tools — a portable DESIGN.md contract plus 468 plugins that make agent output look art-directed rather than auto-generated.

name: Huashu Design
tagline: Agent skill that renders prototypes, decks, MP4 motion and infographics from prompts
description: Huashu Design is an MIT-licensed agent skill that turns a text brief into a finished design deliverable without opening a GUI: clickable HTML prototypes with iPhone/Android/macOS device frames, HTML decks that export to editable PPTX, MP4 and GIF motion at 25 or 60 fps, print-ready infographics as PDF/PNG/SVG, and a five-dimension design critique. It ships a 60-module HTML-native style library — 20 website presets, 20 presentation themes and 20 infographic layouts — all CSS-only, plus a Stage/Sprite animation engine and a deck_stage.js slide engine. A five-step brand-asset protocol makes the agent fetch, download and grep real brand pages for exact colour values instead of guessing them. It is for designers and agent users who want art-directed output rather than the purple-gradient default look.

templates.name: Website style presets
templates.purpose: 20 CSS-only website looks spanning minimal to bold

templates.name: Presentation themes
templates.purpose: 20 deck themes rendered as HTML and exported to editable PPTX

github.last_activity: actively maintained through 2026; relicensed from Personal Use to MIT on 2026-05-14

agent_guidance: Install this when the ask is a polished visual deliverable — a clickable prototype, a deck that must open in PowerPoint, an animated MP4, or an infographic — and you want the output to look art-directed instead of AI-default. Its real value is the 60-module style library and the brand protocol: make it grep the real brand page for colour values rather than recalling a hex, and ask for three parallel variations early so you get batch feedback before committing render time. Pair it with Open Design if you also need a persistent DESIGN.md across projects; keep the optional cloud scripts in /scripts/cloud disabled if the work must stay offline, since the core render path is 100% local.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few agent skills that treats anti-AI-slop as an explicit design constraint, and its PPTX export from computed DOM styles solves the last-mile problem that kills most HTML decks.

name: Guizang PPT Skill
tagline: Agent skill for single-file HTML decks in editorial or Swiss style, plus social covers
description: Guizang PPT Skill is an AGPL-3.0 agent skill that generates horizontal-swipe presentations as one self-contained HTML file, with a built-in presenter mode and rehearsal timing. It ships two locked visual systems: Style A, an editorial-magazine system with 10 layout types (Cover, Section, Data Poster, Image+Text, Image Grid, Pipeline, Comparison and three more) and 5 ink themes; and Style B, Swiss Internationalism with 22 locked layouts (Cover, Statement, KPI Tower, Loop Diagram, Duo Compare, Image Hero, Closing Manifesto and fifteen more) and 4 anchor colours. It also renders slides as images and multi-platform covers at WeChat 21:9, 1:1 share card, Xiaohongshu 3:4 and video-platform landscape. It is for anyone who has to ship a good-looking deck or Chinese-social cover from a prompt.

agent_guidance: Pick this over a general design skill when the deliverable is specifically a deck or a Chinese-social cover and you want a locked grid rather than free layout — the 32 fixed layouts are the point, so choose Style B for numbers-heavy content and Style A for narrative. Two real constraints: it is AGPL-3.0, so do not vendor its CSS into a closed-source product, and its cover presets are tuned for WeChat and Xiaohongshu aspect ratios, which are wrong for LinkedIn or X without adjustment. If you need prototypes, dashboards or video as well, reach for Huashu Design or Open Design instead — this one only makes slides and covers.
why_it_matters: It proves that constraining an agent to a small set of locked layouts produces better decks than letting it lay out freely, and the Swiss system is a genuinely well-drawn reference.

name: Open CoDesign
tagline: MIT desktop app turning prompts into prototypes, slides and PDFs with any model
description: Open CoDesign is an MIT-licensed local-first desktop app that takes a prompt and returns a polished prototype, slide deck, marketing asset or document, exporting to HTML, PDF, PPTX, ZIP and Markdown. It is model-agnostic by design: bring your own key for Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Ollama, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or sign in with a ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription. Version 0.2.0 added agentic design with workspace-backed sessions and local tools. It runs on macOS 12+, Windows 10+ and Linux (glibc 2.31+), and is for people who want a Claude Design alternative that keeps files and model choice on their own machine.
pricing_detail: App is free and MIT. Model cost is yours: BYOK per-token billing, or sign in with an existing ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription.
agent_guidance: Reach for this over Open Design only when the deciding factor is model freedom — it is the one of the two that accepts a ChatGPT Plus/Pro sign-in and any OpenAI-compatible or local Ollama endpoint, so it is the choice when there is no Anthropic key or when everything must run offline. It is also much earlier: at v0.2.0 it has no plugin or template catalog, so you supply the visual direction yourself in the prompt and should not expect brand consistency across sessions. For anything needing a repeatable design system or motion output, use Open Design or Huashu Design instead.
why_it_matters: It is the most model-agnostic of the open Claude Design alternatives, and the only one that lets a plain ChatGPT subscription stand in for an API key.

name: Multica
tagline: Workspace that runs 20 coding-agent CLIs as reviewable teammates
description: Multica is a source-available platform for assigning work to many AI coding agents at once and treating them like teammates: agents pick up issues, report progress and submit work for review inside a shared workspace. It coordinates 20 agent CLIs including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Kimi, Grok and DeepSeek Harness, and adds Squads (agents grouped with humans), Autopilots (scheduled standups, audits and reports) and Skills (reusable playbooks shared across agents). It integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Slack, Lark and DingTalk, and runs as a hosted cloud service, a macOS/Windows/Linux desktop app, an iOS app, or fully self-hosted. It is orchestration infrastructure for human+AI engineering teams rather than a design resource.

github.last_activity: actively maintained (4,778 commits, 804 open issues as of 2026-08)

pricing_detail: Self-hosting is free under the Multica License. Cloud tiers require signup and are not published in the repo. Commercial hosting for third parties needs a separate commercial licence.
agent_guidance: This is workflow infrastructure, not a design resource — reach for it when the problem is coordinating several agent runs across a repo with human review gates, not when you need UI. Read the licence before shipping anything on it: despite the Apache-2.0 base, Part I forbids offering Multica as a hosted service to third parties, forbids removing the logo or product name, and requires user-facing attribution, so it is source-available rather than open source. If you only need one agent on one task, the CLI alone is simpler; Multica earns its weight at squad scale with Autopilots on a schedule.
why_it_matters: It is the most-starred attempt at making multi-agent engineering reviewable rather than chaotic, but its branding and hosting restrictions mean it is not the open-source project the star count suggests.
